capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Estimated: same hardware as MY2017 (the page read); model years compared 2015 to 2017, nothing shows a change. BMW US 2017 release, previous (60 Ah) pack: "22 kWh (gross)/19 kWh (net)".

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: same hardware as MY2017 (the page read); model years compared 2015 to 2017, nothing shows a change. BMW US 2017 release: 60 Ah pack 19 kWh net.
ArenaEV lists 18.8 kWh usable (21.8 gross); Wikipedia infobox 18.2.

chemistry.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia states NMC cells from Samsung SDI; no BMW page read names the chemistry.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: same pack architecture as the 120 Ah car (352 V, BMW US 2019); Wikipedia lists 355 V nominal for the i3 generally. 2014-2018 vs 2019 compared.

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: same hardware as MY2017 (the page read); model years compared 2015 to 2017, nothing shows a change. BMW US 2017 release: BMW Home Charger Connect "can precondition the vehicle battery when connected" and the battery can be warmed before starting off (no navigation trigger or DC-charge trigger described). Read as manual/scheduled only; the 2019 page mentions cabin pre-conditioning and battery warming "under certain conditions". Owner may prefer none.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: same hardware as MY2017 (the page read); model years compared 2015 to 2017, nothing shows a change. BMW US 2017 release "50 kW DC fast charging" for the i3 range; the 60 Ah car has the same CCS system. DC was an option on early cars (see port note).
ArenaEV lists 47 kW max on the 2013 60 Ah car.

ac_max_kw.notes: ArenaEV: 7.4 kW onboard charger; same 7.4 kW on the 94 Ah (BMW US 2017) and 120 Ah (BMW US 2019).
